issues: Keyword 'BOTH' is not the literal terminal word of meaning_story — it's followed by 'held in view'; borderline against strict start/end placement gate, though it is the final clause.

story: A Rice Stalk sways, pierced clean through by a falling Lightning Bolt along the flat Horizon Line, while a Wishbone snaps loose at its foot — swaying wildly, it's quite a RIDE.

story: BEFOREHAND, someone hangs a Looping Fishtail sign on the Wall Peg, ready and waiting long before the doors open.
reading_story: Yo preps everything BEFOREHAND with one short, clipped 'yo' — never caught off guard.

story: The Rake Hand grips one end of the Horizon Line while the Meat Hook grips the other, both hauling opposite ways — the Swaddling Wrap caught helpless in between: pure DISPUTE.

story: The Pot Lid clamps down tight overhead while, beneath it, the two Crossed Axes swap wall-pegs — right blade sliding to the left hook, left blade to the right, blades still up, trading places to MINGLE.

story: Scarecrow stands rigid in the field. A Tape Measure beside him snaps its metal tongue straight out and hooks its tip into his straw sleeve, clamped tight — ADHERE.

reading_story: Ken the doll is propped beside the COW as Exhibit A — his plastic stare makes the whole AFFAIR feel like a tidy, closed-file case.

story: Falling Katana slices straight down onto the War Helmet's crown, driving it hard onto the Scarecrow's head. Pinned in place, it must stand guard forever: RESPONSIBILITY.
reading_story: Ninn wears the War Helmet, jammed on by that same downward blade — nobody else will take the post. She shoulders the RESPONSIBILITY alone.

story: The Sealed Clam-Locket rides down the two Railway Tracks, rail to rail, sliding straight into the Scarecrow's stiff waiting arms — TRANSMIT.
reading_story: Denny hammers spikes into the Railway Tracks, plank by plank, laying the line so it can finally TRANSMIT the locket all the way to the scarecrow.

story: The Scarecrow won't relax — he stands stiffly at attention while a soldier climbs to STAND UP straight on his shoulders, claiming the highest RANK in the field.
reading_story: Mr. Eaton salutes the officer of highest RANK, snapping to attention with a sharp "ee."

story: The stiff Scarecrow at the field's edge holds its straw arms straight out, offering the whole harvest forward to the road — a silent SUBMIT.

story: Scarecrow stands rigid at his post, refusing to leave — one stiff arm clamped tight on the loose strand trailing from Spooled Thread, winding it back so nothing unravels. He's the PERSON IN CHARGE.

story: The Scarecrow never moves, but every word from the Speech Bubble beside it comes true exactly as spoken — nobody has ever caught it lying. That reliability is FAITH.

issues: Speech Bubble's words 'coming true / never caught lying' is a track-record narration rather than a single vivid snapshot image, slightly weakening imageability.
The meaning link (reliable words = faith) is fairly generic/on-the-nose, reducing distinctiveness.

story: Scarecrow stands rigid at the field's edge, watching the sky. A Lightning Bolt cracks straight down beside him, and a Feathered Arrow streaks past, dead level — he reads every sign of the changing WEATHER.
reading_story: Sebastian Coe jogs out to check the sky each dawn, stretching his long "Cooo" as he clocks the WEATHER before every training run.

story: Even a simple straw Scarecrow, carefully mended and painted, can fetch real VALUE at the county fair.
reading_story: Chee haggles hard over the antique's true VALUE, refusing to budge a cent.

story: Every other post in the field stands centered — except one Scarecrow, planted deliberately off to one SIDE.
reading_story: Soaker always parks his cart on the shady SIDE of the street, never the sunny one.

story: Scarecrow stockpiles gear beneath the Rock Overhang: Grass Tuft stuffed in sacks, tools he'll UTILIZE later. Rain can't reach them — he's fully EQUIPPED for whatever the field throws at him.
reading_story: Bee stashes pollen under an overhang before the storm, fully EQUIPPED — every good forager knows preparation beats panic.

story: Scarecrow finally starts to move, dragging its stiff straw legs forward step by step — hard-earned WORK.
reading_story: Jane Doe clocks in early every day, putting in an honest day's WORK.

story: At the annual scarecrow contest, the judges circle once and stop: this one straw Scarecrow, arms out and unmoving, wins first place easily — it doesn't just compete, it EXCELS.
reading_story: Figure skater Yuna glides past every rival with her long, drawn-out 'yuuu' spin — she doesn't just place, she EXCELS.

story: Bean Sprouts poke up from the flat Horizon Line, and beneath them the Wishing-Well Legs kneel, both washed in warm LIGHT.
reading_story: Coe sprints the final stretch, bathed in stadium LIGHT, the crowd roaring his name.

story: A Wishbone splits above the Horizon Line while a Lightning Bolt cracks down between two Railway Tracks, all four shapes locked side by side, standing TOGETHER.

story: Goalpost Frame stands facing the field, its net sagging behind the crossbar. The Stepladder folds flat and tucks itself into that net pocket, hidden deep INSIDE.
reading_story: Nye holds up a diagram of the Goalpost Frame's net pocket, grinning: "The ball is trapped INSIDE — that's just physics, kids!"

story: Tailor's Lapel pins the fabric to the block, and the Cleaver comes down for the very first cut — the BEGINNING of every garment ever made.
reading_story: Shaw watches the tailor's first cut and applauds: "Every masterpiece needs a BEGINNING."

story: A clerk stamps a document, then the Guillotine Blade drops flush against its right edge, slicing it clean in two — final JUDGEMENT.
reading_story: Hancock reviews the split halves and nods once: his JUDGEMENT stands, signed and sealed, no appeal.

story: The Guillotine Blade drops beside the Rice Stalk, slicing the ripe head clean off — the harvested grain sold at market is pure PROFIT.
reading_story: Lee harvests the sliced rice stalk and counts his coins: pure PROFIT.

story: The Guillotine Blade hangs over a cow tied between two Railway Tracks; a Hanging Towel waits ready, and the Falling Katana strikes first — this abattoir runs by strict SYSTEM.
reading_story: Old Sage inspects every step of the SYSTEM with his slow, drawn-out voice, making sure nothing runs out of order.

story: The Guillotine Blade drops clean through the middle of the loaf, splitting it evenly in two — a perfect DIVIDE.
reading_story: Cutler counts to three, then in one clean stroke, he'll DIVIDE the cake exactly in half.

story: Open Mouth roars a battle-cry down onto Flexing Bicep below — the shout itself pours strength into the muscle, swelling it bigger. Voice plus power: ADD.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr barks a short "ka!" out his window at a rival cab cutting him off — sharp, clipped, gone in an instant. ADD an enemy to Carr's list.
issues: Imageability is borderline: 'shout pours strength into muscle, swelling it' is a causal/synesthetic leap rather than a directly picturable single action — works as a cartoon panel but requires inferring an invisible transfer of energy.
Distinctiveness is generic: 'voice/shout powers up a muscle' is a stock battle-cry trope not tightly anchored to the specific 口-over-力 layout of 加; could be reused for many unrelated kanji pairs.

story: The Watching Eye spots a hiker collapsed on the trail, unblinking, missing nothing — instantly the Flexing Bicep swoops in, scooping the hiker up to HELP.
reading_story: Jo sprints in when the Watching Eye signals distress, muscles ready — everyone in town knows Jo is the one who'll always HELP.

story: Three tiny BEAN SPROUTS push up under a white BEDSHEET COVER draped over the field, while a FLEXING BICEP strains beneath the cloth, hauling — that's LABOR.
reading_story: Rowe pulls a bedsheet cover off the strained bicep after his shift: pure LABOR, Rowe grunts.

story: A Trailing Footprint is stamped in the dirt, marking where someone quit — but a Flexing Bicep strains behind it, refusing to lift, holding the ground alone. Someone must finish the TASK.
reading_story: The Flexing Bicep trembles, veins standing out with one clipped grunt — "Moo." That single strain is the whole TASK.

story: The Full Moon glows low behind Twin Pillars at the finish line — and a Flexing Bicep punches skyward between them, arm raised in pure triumph: VICTORY.
reading_story: Showman bursts through the Twin Pillars roaring "Shoooow!", raising his fist for the crowd's VICTORY.

story: CHANGE: overnight, the farmer swears the Scarecrow standing stiff in his field got swapped — now it's just a giant Soup Ladle jammed in the dirt, tilted at the exact same watching angle.

story: Beneath the Rock Overhang, a White Candle burns, its wax pooling into a Sand Trickle that spreads wide across open ground — a boundless MEADOW.
reading_story: Glenn surveys his original MEADOW — the very first field he ever claimed, standing proud at its primitive, untouched edge.

story: Above a still Horizon Line, a Sealed Clam-Locket hovers shut — private, unopened. Beside it, three Comb Streaks rake diagonally downward, dragging travel-trails across the sky toward the horizon: footprints of someone about to VISIT.
reading_story: Santa drops down the chimney to VISIT every house at once — three comb-streak sleigh trails raked across the sky mark exactly where he's been.
issues: Actor consistency (gate 5, borderline pass): registry persona for 彡 Comb Streaks is 'raked left to right' through hair/paint; story reassigns them as 'rake diagonally downward' forming 'travel-trails' / 'footprints' / then reading_story calls them 'sleigh trails' — direction and role shift across the two stories. This is ordinary physical motion (a streak-actor leaving a trail), not an invented cognitive faculty, so it stays inside the allowed motion license, but the persona's stated left-to-right raking direction is contradicted.

Imageability capped at 3: the story stacks three metaphors for the same streaks (travel-trails -> footprints -> someone about to visit) rather than committing to one clean image, and 'hovers shut' gives the clam-locket no clear spatial anchor relative to the horizon line.

Minor: story's closing clause 'footprints of someone about to VISIT' introduces an implicit unnamed 'someone' actor distinct from the three named components — not a phantom component per se (no new glyph-actor claimed) but slightly muddies which actor is doing the visiting.

story: A Rock Overhang stands firm — but a Rubber Glove flops down flat across it, palm-out, covering the stone the wrong way round: ANTI-.
reading_story: Hancock slaps his signature palm-print onto the wall ANTI- the king's decree, backwards and defiant.
issues: Rubber Glove's defined image is 'palm-up, fingers loosely curled' but the story describes it landing 'palm-out' — a minor contradiction of the actor's own defined orientation, not a fabricated new action but a fidelity slip worth tightening.
'Flops down' introduces slight motion not present in the static 'lying palm-up' image description; low severity, still recognizably the same object/pose family.

story: A lightning bolt cracks straight down and lands right in the rubber glove's open upturned palm below, sitting there like a caught ball. The glove just holds what fell into it. OBTAIN.
reading_story: A cobbler named Shoe hammers all day, and at closing time customers line up to pay him — coins piling into his open palm as he moves to OBTAIN, OBTAIN, OBTAIN, one per finished shoe.

story: Hawk Talon reaches down through the Bedsheet Cover draped between them, dropping a parcel straight into the waiting Rubber Glove below — the glove closes: ACCEPT.
reading_story: Juju stretches out her Rubber Glove hand under the sheet-covered talon delivery and grins as she is the first to ACCEPT it.

story: The Stepladder stands over the Horizon Line, planting one leg on each side, and lowers its peak into the Open Mouth below — a perfect FIT.
reading_story: General Gough drills the pieces together — stepladder over line, tip into mouth — until they FIT just right, barking a long, drawn-out 'Gō!'

story: Bricked into a wall, the Goalpost Frame stands as a window's edge, and inside it an Open Mouth juts out, chin over the sill, hollering YONDER at someone across the street.
reading_story: Coe leans out that same window frame, cups his hands, and bellows toward the YONDER finish line — his voice carrying farther than any sprint he's run.

story: A Falling Katana slices straight down through a Mound of Soil, cracking it wide open to reveal an Open Mouth screaming out a REVELATION.
reading_story: Coker bursts into the newsroom and slams the mound of evidence on the desk: this REVELATION goes public right now.

story: An Open Mouth shouts across the field while a Flapping Pennant snaps in the wind beside it, signaling everyone to CALL back.
reading_story: Coco cups her hands and lets out a long CALL across the canyon, waiting for the echo.

story: Atop the Stepladder, over the flat Horizon Line, an Open Mouth bellows a decree down to the kneeling Wax Stamp, which presses down hard, sealing your FATE.
reading_story: Theresa May reads out the decree: 'By royal seal, this is your FATE!' The Wax Stamp presses down hard, her long ē echoing as it seals.

story: Rice Stalk sways left in the breeze, and Open Mouth beside it bursts into song, timing every shout to match the stalk's swing exactly — two different bodies, one perfect rhythm: HARMONY.

issues: Minor: Open Mouth's image is defined as 'lips parted as if mid-shout,' but the story has it 'burst into song' before circling back to 'shout' — the singing verb is a slight extension beyond the defined action, though 'shout' is also explicitly used in the same sentence so it stays tethered to the source image.

story: Inside the Goalpost Frame's stall, propped to stand up on its Wishing-Well Legs, a cart's Open Mouth cries out today's prices — the mark of a busy MERCHANT.
reading_story: The Showman barks his pitch louder than anyone, the sharpest MERCHANT on the block.

story: Walled Box's four stone walls have no gate — Open Mouth shouts inside, and the cry bounces wall to wall, unable to escape, echoing back on itself again and again: -TIMES.
reading_story: Trapped in that same echoing Walled Box, Open Mouth's cry keeps bouncing back as "Kai! Kai! Kai!" — the surfer's name ricocheting -TIMES off the stone.

story: Under the blazing Sun, the Rice-Paddy Grid keeps gaining new squares while a Mound of Soil piles higher against the Twin Pillars' base — the whole field can only INCREASE.
reading_story: Zoe's flock just keeps growing — more chicks hatch every morning, numbers only ever INCREASE, she says with a long, drawn-out 'zooo.'

story: The War Helmet tips forward and CLANGS down hard onto the Draped Cloak's slumped shoulders — metal ringing out sharp over limp fabric. That ringing clang is a VOICE.
reading_story: Sage lets his War Helmet slip and clang against the floor — "sei," he sighs, long and low — even a dropped helmet has a VOICE.

story: You lift the Pot Lid expecting dinner still bubbling inside — but the pot itself is gone, replaced by one muddy Trailing Footprint leading off into the dark. STRANGE.
reading_story: Henson keeps humming the Muppet theme as he stirs — then notices his own hand has become a Trailing Footprint print on the floor. "Huh, that's STRANGE," he mutters, unbothered.

story: The Stepladder stands tall, pinned through by two crossing Railway Tracks, arms spread wide like a Starfish — the strong figure of a HUSBAND.
reading_story: Foo Fighter grins, ring on his finger, a proud short 'fu' — every inch the doting HUSBAND.

story: A Falling Katana slices clean through the rope the husband was carrying — in one stroke, he stands to LOSE it all.

story: Hourglass leans close to cradle the Swaddle Basket, rocking it tenderly — she's utterly FOND of the child inside.
reading_story: Coe jogs past the Hourglass and the Swaddle Basket, grinning — he's FOND of this peaceful family scene.

story: Beneath the Thatched House's peaked roof, a Falling Katana rests flat along the Horizon Line, and a Fishhook hangs quiet on the wall — everything safely tucked at HOME.
reading_story: Tucker kicks off his boots and sighs — nothing beats walking into his own HOME.

story: Under the Thatched House's low eaves, the Tape Measure stretches its quivering tongue flat across the threshold, marking the one narrow inch anyone may step through. GUARD.
reading_story: Master Shu crouches under that same thatched eave each dawn, checking the Tape Measure's inch-mark himself before anyone passes — short, clipped, exact. He'll GUARD the threshold.

story: Under the Thatched House's sloping eaves, an Open Mouth barks endless orders at everyone sheltered beneath it: the roof protects only those who obey the BUREAUCRAT.
reading_story: Genghis KHAN gallops beneath the Thatched House's roof, demanding tribute — the BUREAUCRAT's Open Mouth echoes his orders to everyone sheltered inside.

story: The Thatched House drops its peaked cap straight over the Fabric Roll below, pinning the loose trailing end under its eaves so no more cloth can unspool: DETERMINE.
reading_story: Tay measures cloth for a living: once the Thatched House caps a Fabric Roll's trailing foot, Tay marks the length in his ledger — DETERMINE.

story: Beneath the Thatched House's sloped roof, a War Helmet sits propped on its stand — and under that, a Starfish sprawls flat, arms flung wide across the floorboards. No illusions here: this is REALITY.
reading_story: Jitter shakes the War Helmet loose, spills the Starfish out from under the Thatched House roof — proof this whole scene is REALITY, not a dream.

story: Thatched House roof slams down, Pot Lid clamps beneath it, crushing the Mound of Soil flat, squeezing until the buried Open Mouth chokes and screams — pure HARM.
reading_story: Guy digs through the crushed Mound of Soil to free the choking mouth, muttering that this house causes nothing but HARM.
issues: Story stacks four sequential physical actions (roof slams, lid clamps, soil crushes, mouth screams) which is slightly dense to picture as one image, though still coherent.
Reading_story reuses 'crushed Mound of Soil' and repeats the keyword HARM, a minor redundancy but not disqualifying.

story: The Twin Ski Slopes crash down into their notch, spilling snow everywhere — until the Thatched House drops overhead, its eaves scooping every last flake inward. Now it can CONTAIN it.
reading_story: Ask Yoyo to pack for a trip: he lowers his cello case's lid over shirts piled past the brim, pressing until it shuts — that case can barely CONTAIN it all.

story: Under the Thatched House's roof, a Rubber Glove points up at the Crescent Moon, using hand signals to show what tomorrow's weather will be — nothing but a GUESS.
reading_story: Satcher squints at the tea leaves and makes his best GUESS, muttering a clipped 'satsu' under his breath.

story: A SENTENCE stands printed on the left page; facing it on the right, the Tape Measure unspools itself, tongue quivering, stretching to match it line for line, mirror for mirror. OPPOSITE.
reading_story: Ty Cobb slides in hard, clipped and short, straight at the catcher blocking home plate — two men OPPOSITE, neither giving ground.

story: In a cramped BUREAU, a Draped Cloak slumps behind the desk, its hood gaping into an Open Mouth that barks stamps-and-forms orders at the line.
reading_story: Kyoker storms into the BUREAU, slamming his stamp down short and sharp — kyoku, kyoku, kyoku — demanding every form be sealed before lunch.

story: Falling Katana slashes clean between the Woolly Ram's fleece and the I-Beam Girder below — one clearly wool, one clearly steel: an unmistakable DISTINCTION.
reading_story: Sah measures the gap the katana cut, calling out each DISTINCTION between ram and girder in one short breath.

story: Under the clamped-down Pot Lid, a Hanging Towel sways above rows of stalls — welcome to the CITY market square.
reading_story: Sheriff patrols the stalls beneath the Pot Lid roof, badge gleaming, keeping peace across the whole CITY.

story: Under the Cliff Awning's slanted shade, someone drapes the Hanging Towel flat on the ground like a mat and sits down — claiming this spot as their SEAT.
reading_story: Sekka the chef finds every SEAT taken at the counter, so she spreads her own towel on a crate and eats standing over it instead.
issues: Reading_story reuses the towel motif from the main story rather than referencing Sekka's canonical ladle-flip action from the registry note — she's still recognizably 'the chef' so this doesn't break the actor-consistency gate, but it's a missed opportunity for a more distinct reading-story beat.

Distinctiveness is good but not top-tier: 'shelter providing shade + cloth laid down as a seat/mat' is a fairly ordinary scene template that could blend with other cloth- or shelter-themed component stories.

story: Under a Bedsheet Cover, three Bean Sprouts poke up every single day, always into the same yawning Open Mouth, above the same Hanging Towel drying in its USUAL spot — nothing ever changes.
reading_story: Average Joe stretches "Joooe" every morning at the same bus stop, same coffee, same seat — Joe is nothing if not USUAL.
issues: Minor spatial inconsistency: story places Hanging Towel (巾) as if below/separate ('above the same Hanging Towel') when in the actual glyph 巾 sits at the base with the other three components stacked on top as 尚; not a gating violation since no component is invented or omitted, but slightly weakens the visual coherence.
The causal link between the four images (sprouts growing under a cover, into a mouth, near a towel) feels somewhat assembled/collage-like rather than one unified scene, capping imageability at 3.

story: The ANTENNA MAST leans level, resting its long bar across the Twin Pillars' shared ledge — perfectly balanced, perfectly FLAT.
reading_story: Hayes surveys the flat plain and declares it FLAT — level ground fit for any building.

story: The I-Beam Girder lies flat as the altar table, and the Ritual Stake is driven slantwise beside it into the earth, sacred rope trailing from its dart-notch — every priest sets his tools this exact way: that is STYLE.
reading_story: Shicker counts the coda -ki like a bell: girder down, stake in — same order every time, and Shicker calls that order STYLE.

story: The Longbow clamps one end of a Lightning Bolt in its grip and hauls it straight back into a taut line, bending its own belly hard to PULL.
reading_story: Quinn grabs the taut Lightning Bolt like a rope and gives a short, sharp in-tug — just enough to PULL it loose.

story: Rake Hand scrapes flat across three Bean Sprouts below — every stroke lands square on target. HIT.
reading_story: Tone drops the mic and it falls dead center on the sprouts — a clean HIT, right on cue.

story: Cupped Palms hold the clay steady while three Comb Streaks rake grooves across it, and a final Falling Katana slice trims the edge — the pot takes SHAPE.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer poses just so, her silhouette taking perfect SHAPE under the spotlight.

story: On the Forked Footpath a conscript is seized -- an officer tightens the Lance-Butt Grip on his shoulder, drafting him for war. This is his DUTY.
reading_story: Yakker barks roll call at the barracks gate, listing every man's DUTY for the war campaign -- yak, yak, yak, his voice cracks like a whip.

story: Down the Forked Footpath, past the Horizon Sunrise, a hand pulls out the Tape Measure to claim exactly what was earned — pure GAIN.
reading_story: Toker counts his GAIN in short, clipped puffs — 'toku, toku' — never taking more than his measured share.

story: Falling Katana slices diagonally into the top of a HEART — one clean cut through its core. Wound this deep is CERTAIN, invariably fatal.
reading_story: The Hitcher hitchhikes with a knife-scarred HEART pinned to his jacket — CERTAIN proof of the ride that marked him.

story: Living only in the NOW, no memory of past or future, this HEART obsesses over one single WISH, over and over.
reading_story: Nenn kneels before his HEART's shrine, chanting the same WISH again and again — Nenn only ever prays for the now.

story: NATURE: Twin Candle Wicks stand side by side on the ledge, each flame trembling to its own private heartbeat — one twitchy, one calm — never swapping rhythms.
reading_story: Sage leans close to the ledge, counting each wick's trembling beat on his fingers, and declares every private rhythm pure NATURE before it even flickers.

story: Twin Candle Wicks sit on the left ledge, one flame roaring with joy, the other guttering in grief — both burning at once, impossible to separate. That trembling double blaze is FEELINGS.
reading_story: Joe stares at the Twin Candle Wicks until his throat tightens — Joooe, he groans, dragging the vowel out long, drowning in raw FEELINGS he can't name.

story: Staring inward at nothing, eyes unfocused, you sink beneath thought entirely — until a single CONCEPT surfaces from the quiet dark of your heart, glowing.
reading_story: Sosa steps to the plate, but before swinging he pictures the whole play in his head — a perfect CONCEPT of the home run, rehearsed in his heart first.
issues: meaning_placement is labeled 'end' but CONCEPT is not the literal final word of the story ('...CONCEPT surfaces from the quiet dark of your heart, glowing.') — it's in the climactic clause but followed by a trailing phrase; acceptable as loosely 'end-positioned' but worth tightening in future generations.

story: Falling Katana slices one clean mark above an Open Mouth crying out; below, a heart pounds while a planted Barbed Pike stands sentinel over it all — pure EMOTION.
reading_story: Genghis Khan roars from his horse, flooded with raw EMOTION as his army cries out behind him.

story: The Barbed Pike stands planted, hooked spur catching the light — then the Falling Katana slices clean down across it, its silver slash overwriting the spur's silhouette: same pike, new shape, TURN INTO.
reading_story: Sage stands over the newly-slashed pike, stroking his white beard, drawing the sound long: "seeee..." he intones, "it will TURN INTO something else now."

story: Lone Barn Shutter creaks alone on its hinge beside the doorway, and right next to it Woodsman Hatchet stands buried in its block — mark this exact PLACE.
reading_story: Shaw pauses at that same doorway, hatchet embedded just beside him, and says: this PLACE is mine.

story: The Grabber Claw lowers from the left, fingers snatching the dangling Meat Hook off its rail, and swings the heavy iron barb downward to STRIKE the counter with a metallic crack.
reading_story: Dah! — the Grabber Claw slams the Meat Hook home on every STRIKE, the short heavy thud echoing "Dah" through the butcher shop.

story: THROW: the GRABBER CLAW lowers, closes its fingers around the LANCE-BUTT GRIP's fist itself, and swings the whole clenched fist backward then forward, releasing it to sail through the air.
reading_story: TONE winds up a long, looping pitch and lets the ball fly with a drawn-out THROW, his name echoing as it arcs away.
issues: Minor clarity issue (non-gating): the claw grabs 'the Lance-Butt Grip's fist itself' rather than acting on the lance/pole, which slightly blurs the two distinct actors into one swung mass rather than showing a clear claw+lance interaction.

story: A three-fingered Grabber Claw hangs at the left edge, its half-clenched digits lowering to snatch a prize — each separate digit is exactly one FINGER.
reading_story: Sheriff barks a clipped "shi" and levels one accusing FINGER at the suspect across the saloon.

story: A Rubber Glove hand grips the pole below a Plus-Sign Crossroads, holding it steady like a scaffold — that single hand BRANCH bears the whole structure's weight.
reading_story: Sheriff braces the leaning signpost with one flat hand, propping the BRANCH upright before it topples into the crossroads.
issues: Minor: the story introduces staging nouns not in the component list ('the pole', 'scaffold') — acceptable as scene-setting, not phantom component actors, but keep an eye on this pattern drifting toward implied extra objects.
Distinctiveness is only middling: 'hand propping up a support/pole' is a fairly generic support-image trope that could blend with other branch/support/prop kanji mnemonics.

story: Cracking Whip lashes the leash right off the dog's collar — one crack and the animal bolts free across the yard. SET FREE.
reading_story: Ho, watching from his sleigh, laughs as the reindeer are SET FREE from their harness and bound into the snow.

story: A Cracking Whip snaps down, again and again, driving a whole nation into marching line-step: this relentless rap-and-drive rules them — POLITICS.
reading_story: Sage draws the whip's rhythm out long, せーい, stretching each crack like his own bearded drawl — that long note is POLITICS.

story: The Cracking Whip lashes down on the Cowrie Shell, its ridged slit splitting clean apart — coins scatter uselessly across the floor. Treasure ruined in one strike: FAILURE.
reading_story: Hyde smashes another Cowrie Shell underfoot out of spite, gloating at each FAILURE he causes.

story: Hourglass streams sand, marking each passing beat, as Cracking Whip snaps behind it — driving Scattered Rice Grains to leap forward one by one, each crack adding another grain to the growing pile. NUMBER.
reading_story: Soo drips sand grain by grain, stretching each beat long and slow — patiently building the NUMBER, one long ū at a time.

story: Scattered Rice Grains lie piled on the flat Horizon Line — Lightning Bolt cracks straight down through the pile, splitting it into two heaps. Woodsman Hatchet chops the gap wider. DECLINE: severed, no reunion.
reading_story: Dan stands at the Horizon Line's two rice heaps and won't push them back together — he'll DECLINE, letting the split stand.

story: Beside the blazing midday Sun, Falling Katana slices one clean diagonal slash, then Lightning Bolt cracks straight down right next to it — two strokes pinned side by side on the Sun's flank, crossing it out: YESTERDAY.
reading_story: Sacco the anarchist pins his diagonal Falling-Katana-style calling card to the wall — dated, already crossed out. He struck YESTERDAY, saku, and vanished before dawn.

story: The blazing Sun climbs over the rooftops, painting the whole valley gold — postcard-perfect SCENERY.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer stops mid-step, dazzled by the golden valley SCENERY spread below the stage.

story: A Candy Tin sits sealed beneath the Full Moon; when the treat inside snaps like a Wishbone, one PERIOD has ended and the next begins.
reading_story: Key locks away one PERIOD's candy tin with a short, clipped 'ki' before starting the count again.

story: Tree stretches its two branches upward, straining higher — until Horizon Line clamps flat across their very ends, sealing off the topmost TIP.
reading_story: Matsu balances on the narrowest TIP of the tree's highest branch, arms out, refusing to climb one inch further.

story: Lightning Bolt cracks straight down through the flooded Rice-Paddy Grid, striking the Tree's crown until its branches swell and burst into heavy, round FRUIT.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr pulls up under the tree, and a crate of ripe FRUIT tumbles straight into his cab.

story: A single Tree stands fixed in its social rank among the forest — its height, its bark, its very STATUS never changes.
reading_story: Knuckles the boxer fights his way up in rank, punch by punch, climbing the STATUS ladder one bout at a time.

story: Tree trunk planted beside an empty Goalpost Frame; inside it, the Horizon Line rests flat above the Plus-Sign Crossroads — scaffolding braced upright for good POSTURE.
reading_story: Coe stretches into perfect POSTURE at the starting line, spine straight as scaffolding, before the gun fires.

story: A single Tree stands unmoved as a Tsunami Wave crashes past it — that calm, unshaken poise is its own MANNER.
reading_story: Yoyo the cellist bows with practiced MANNER, never rushing a single note.

story: Stumpy Sparrow perches atop the bare Tree, ruling the yard — until a Feathered Arrow thuds into the trunk beside him, and every bird obeys the one who claims that branch. AUTHORITY.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll plants the Feathered Arrow at the Tree's base like a flagpole of AUTHORITY, and Stumpy Sparrow salutes from the top branch.

story: The Tree, always standing straight, gets shoved clean off its roots and topples — SIDEWAYS, trunk flat along the ground, branches pointing off to the side.
reading_story: Owen the keeper paces the fallen orchard row, sighing at every trunk lying SIDEWAYS, muttering a long "ōōōwen" as he counts the toppled trees.

story: At the gate you must STOP: a Barbed Pike blocks the path, a Falling Katana slashes one notch into its shaft, and a Sand Trickle drains through the cut — another year of AGE marked.
reading_story: Cy notches the pike himself each birthday, counting slashes to know his AGE — さい, short and clipped as the blade-strike.

story: A Falling Katana slices past a Duster Wisp and one Ink Droplet, leaving only a Gnawed Rib-Bone behind — the sorry REMAINDER.
reading_story: Zann counts the coins left in his pocket — the meager REMAINDER after rent.

story: A jagged Lightning Bolt strikes straight down, notch by notch, onto the Lance-Butt Grip's raised fist — each jolt carving one more level. Climb the jagged STEPS.
reading_story: Dan counts each notch as the bolt carves downward — "one, two" — climbing the jagged STEPS to the top.
issues: Lance-Butt Grip is largely passive (just 'raised fist' receiving strikes) rather than actively using its defined nature of gripping/jabbing a lance — borderline persona fit, though not an invented cognitive ability so it doesn't fail gating.
The lightning bolt 'carving' notches into levels is a slightly abstract causal mechanism (lightning doesn't naturally notch/carve), which caps imageability rather than making it vivid.

story: A Family Crest Banner snaps over the village gate while every Open Mouth beneath it roars the same clan name in unison — that roaring crowd are the PEOPLE.
reading_story: Minn plants the Family Crest Banner in the square and shouts through cupped hands until the whole PEOPLE echoes his cry back.

story: Above a flat desert HORIZON LINE, a TSUNAMI WAVE curls and crashes down desperately, one INK DROPLET splashing off its crest — the wave's whole violent motion is a REQUEST for the shore.
reading_story: Governor CUOMO stands before the crashing wave, arms out, shouting his REQUEST for aid — kyū, long ū, echoing over the water.

story: On the Railway Tracks, Stepladder stands planted on its two splayed legs. Above it, Starfish sprawls across the top rung, arms flung wide toward both rails at once. Puddle Splash flicks its droplets left, scattering down beside them: DECIDE.
reading_story: Ketel, vodka man, straddles the Railway Tracks' two rails — one boot each — and raises his bottle: DECIDE, he toasts, savoring that short -tsu snap on his tongue.

story: Puddle Splash flicks her three droplets left across the pedestal's flat top, smoothing every wobble flat and still: whoever holds the calmed PEDESTAL holds the REIGN.
reading_story: Chee, clipped and short, steps onto the still pedestal Puddle Splash just smoothed and claims her quiet REIGN — no fuss, no flames, just chee.

story: Puddle Splash flicks her three droplets leftward, watching water always LEAVE by the same slope, same speed, same spot — that unchanging drainage is the METHOD.
reading_story: Santa Ho tests the icy slope himself, ho-ho-ho — sliding off at the exact same spot every time. Same slope, same spot: that's his METHOD.

story: Puddle Splash leaps and dances across the pavement, flicking droplets everywhere with wild, restless energy — utterly LIVELY.
reading_story: Cutler claps his hands sharply — katsu! — and the whole room springs LIVELY awake at his short, clipped command.

story: Puddle Splash flicks droplets left as Pot Lid clamps down on Sealed Clam-Locket, forcing it to squeeze out and join River Rapids rushing downhill — everything swept into the CURRENT.
reading_story: Ryu rides the CURRENT downstream, long ū howling as rapids drag him past the clamped lid and locket toward the sea.
issues: Causal link 'Pot Lid clamps down on Sealed Clam-Locket, forcing it to squeeze out' is a somewhat forced/confusing physical interaction between two static personas (a lid and a locket) — passes as ordinary physical motion but weakens image clarity rather than sharpening it.

story: Puddle Splash hurls her three droplets rightward, soaking Bean Sprouts on top and the Full Moon below — glow, sprouts, and shine all drowned out at once: EXTINGUISH.
reading_story: Showman bellows "Shoooow's over!" and yanks the switch — every spotlight on the Full Moon backdrop goes black: EXTINGUISH.

story: Puddle Splash trickles past a sunken Tree, down past the Wishing-Well Legs, vanishing beneath the Bedsheet Cover into the DEEP dark below.
reading_story: Shinn dives DEEP off the pier, vanishing beneath the surface in one clean plunge.

story: Puddle Splash flicks three droplets onto your unpaid bill, dissolving every red number until the page runs clear — the debt is finally SETTLED.
reading_story: Cy signs the last check, and Puddle Splash rinses the ink away — the whole account is SETTLED, clean as Cy's pitching mound.

story: Under the Cliff Awning, someone lays the empty Rubber Glove flat as a stepping-plank across the Puddle Splash — you hop palm to palm, dry-footed, in swift TRANSIT.
reading_story: Toto trots palm to palm over the glove-plank, splashing nothing, first across in every TRANSIT.

story: Puddle Splash sprays droplets into the Wellhead Grid's square basin. Wishbone snaps apart to widen the gap, but Stop Barrier drops flat, sealing ships safely inside: the HARBOR.
reading_story: Coe jogs the docks at dawn, lungs full of salt air, and cheers as the first ferry glides into the HARBOR right on schedule.

story: Lightning Bolt cracks past the Horizon Line as Puddle Splash floods over the Railway Tracks, rising past the Goalpost Frame until it laps the Mountain Peak — the whole valley FULL.
reading_story: Mann surveys the reservoir, brimming FULL to the very top of the dam.

story: Beneath the Thatched House roof, Puddle Splash floods the Rice-Paddy Grid, until Wishbone kicks its legs apart at the bottom, spraying water in a wild PERFORMANCE.
reading_story: Enzo Ferrari swerves onto the flooded rice-paddy stage, tires splashing water everywhere as the crowd roars at his reckless PERFORMANCE.
issues: Wishbone's action 'spraying water' is not part of its defined persona (mid-snap, legs splitting) — allowed as ordinary physical extrapolation of the splitting motion, but it's a stretch and slightly weakens persona fidelity.
Main story's spatial logic is a bit muddled (thatched house roof over a flooding paddy with a wishbone at 'the bottom') — hurts imageability slightly.
Distinctiveness is only moderate — a generic 'splashing water performance' scene, not a sharply memorable image.

story: The COAL BRAZIER burns low, its four coals scorching the floorboards beneath — when it's dragged away, each coal leaves behind one charred SPOT.
reading_story: Detective Tennison crouches by the scorched floorboards with his magnifying glass, circling the exact SPOT where the brazier once stood.

story: Under Crescent Moon, a dog turns on the Coal Brazier's spit, smoke swallowing its shape till onlookers can only call it: SORT OF THING.
reading_story: Master Zen sniffs the smoke drifting from the fire pit and rules, with total calm: "SORT OF THING. Sit. Eat. Do not ask which thing."

story: Split Bed-Plank props up a cot, and a DOG sprawls across it, refusing to move — this exact sprawl is the STATUS QUO, unchanged night after night.
reading_story: Every morning Joe finds the dog still sprawled on the bed-plank, sighs "Joooe, same as always" — the STATUS QUO holds.

story: A woman leaps up to STAND UP, banging her head on the Rock Overhang above — the shock sends her doubling over, and beneath the ledge a Sprouting Plant's leaf pushes free of the dirt: she's about to GIVE BIRTH.
reading_story: Santa ducks under the Rock Overhang's low stone lip, arriving just as the mother starts to GIVE BIRTH, and holds her hand through every contraction.
issues: Main story is exactly 40 words — at the outer edge of the '≤ ~40 words' length gate, no margin left.
Story stacks four sequential micro-actions (leap up → bang head → double over → plant sprouts) into one 'moment,' which dilutes peak imageability versus a single clean snapshot.
The unnamed 'woman' is a generic story subject enacting 立 (which has no defined actor/image), not a phantom kanji component — acceptable, but worth flagging as a borderline convention.

story: A Lightning Bolt strikes straight down through the Rice-Paddy Grid, punching clean through its mud dikes and stabbing out the bottom — witnesses point at the scorch line, demanding WHEREFORE.
reading_story: Yuna the figure skater carves one long ū-groove clean through the ice, and judges lean in asking WHEREFORE she cut that exact line.

story: A Lightning Bolt pierces straight down through the midday Sun into the Rice-Paddy Grid below — with deep respect, I HAVE THE HONOR TO speak.
reading_story: Shinn bows low and says he'd HAVE THE HONOR TO join the ceremony.

story: Badger Paw-Print stamps down, claw by claw, onto one square of the Rice-Paddy Grid — then hops to the next square, patiently taking its TURN on every plot in line.
reading_story: Bann calls out the plot numbers as the badger stamps each square — "Bann, next!" — announcing whose TURN it is.

story: A Fabric Roll unspools crookedly; a Feathered Arrow misses its mark; a Soup Ladle drips the wrong way; even the Wall Peg looks crooked — nothing here inspires anything but DOUBT.
reading_story: Gee squints hard at the crooked peg and mutters a short, clipped 'gi' — pure DOUBT in his voice.

story: The Plus-Sign Crossroads sits dead center, the Watching Eye stares straight down through it, the Lightning Bolt cracks straight down through the eye's stare, landing exactly on the Horizon Line below — all four FIXED in one plumb vertical.
reading_story: Choker stands where the Lightning Bolt struck the Horizon Line, plants his boots on the exact mark, chyoku, and won't budge — he is FIXED to that one straight spot.

story: A Tree stands still while a giant Watching Eye hovers over its crown, and the Tree stares right back — two silent witnesses locked in MUTUAL gaze.
reading_story: Sosa leans on the Tree's trunk under that same Watching Eye, nodding at it — respect flows MUTUAL both ways, player to eye.

story: Under a cliff, the OPEN MOUTH shouts down at the squat grey BOULDER wedged below — its echo bounces off cold, immovable STONE.
reading_story: Sekka the chef flips his ladle once against the doorstep STONE, testing its ring — seki, solid stone.

story: Under the Thatched House's cap, Stumpy Sparrow grips the roof-beam and hops his full weight onto it three times — it doesn't creak, doesn't dip. Beside him, Boulder sits wedged as the doorstop that never rolls: ASSURANCE.
reading_story: Knuckles the boxer bear-hugs the Thatched House's beam and yanks — his knuckles whiten, the beam won't budge an inch. ASSURANCE.

story: Two Railway Tracks lie flat side by side; a Sand Trickle falls straight down between them, landing right at the junction where anyone walking past cannot help but look down and see it. SHOW.
reading_story: Jee walks the Railway Tracks, spots the fresh Sand Trickle pile at his feet, and points down at it to SHOW the crew where to dig.

story: A lone Roadside Shrine stands at the crossroads, offerings piled at its foot — sacred ground, watched over by the GODS.
reading_story: Shinn kneels before the shrine, praying quietly to the GODS for safe travels.

story: At the Roadside Shrine on the Horizon Line, an Open Mouth gives thanks over the bountiful Rice-Paddy Grid — harvest season, a true BLESSING.
reading_story: Fokker counts his lucky stars, calling the whole harvest a rare BLESSING.

story: Farmer paces off his rice paddy in exact strides, marking boundary stakes at each measured step — the RICE STALK field defines the precise EXTENT.
reading_story: Tay measures the rice field's EXTENT stride by stride, calling out numbers as his long paces map the paddy's edge.

story: Each Rice Stalk grown here is tagged and catalogued by its exact SPECIES.
reading_story: Shu the botanist labels every new SPECIES with careful, precise handwriting.

story: A big Starfish arm shoots straight into the Burrow Hole, spearing deep in one sudden STAB.
reading_story: Totter lunges forward with a single STAB of his cane, catching his balance just in time.

story: A farmer's hand flings Scattered Rice Grains high — they hang in the air a heartbeat, a perfect cross of white against the sky: RICE.
reading_story: Michael BAY yells 'cut!' so loud the granary bursts, spraying RICE everywhere in his booming, drawn-out voice.

story: PROMISE: the Spooled Thread's loose strand loops right through the Sugar Scoop's hooked handle, cinching tight — its trapped sugar grain sealing the vow shut.
reading_story: Yakker swears his PROMISE, hooking his little finger through hers like thread caught in a scoop's curled handle, sealing the deal.

story: Workers hoist crates onto shelves in neat rows and columns while the Spooled Thread's loose strand loops from crate to crate, lashing every stack together to ASSEMBLE the warehouse racks.
reading_story: Saul walks the warehouse floor clipboard in hand, tagging each rack as workers ASSEMBLE it, checking off rows one short "so" at a time.

story: The Rubber Glove smooths a Spooled Thread taut across a Mound of Soil, tracing one unbroken line from start to end — a sacred SUTRA.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer traces the thread's long line with her fingertip, humming a slow, drawn-out 'kei' as she reads the SUTRA aloud.

story: The Spooled Thread unspools endlessly across the counter where a merchant tries to SELL — every time he cuts it, another loose strand keeps feeding through, forcing him to CONTINUE.
reading_story: Zocker keeps betting hand after hand, refusing to stop — he'll CONTINUE playing until the whole table goes home.

story: Fishermen lower the wide FISHING NET flat over the water, letting it settle exactly where it lands — careful PLACEMENT decides which fish get trapped below.
reading_story: Chee lowers the FISHING NET with a short, clipped snap of her wrist — precise PLACEMENT, no wasted motion, "chee" and done.

story: A prize Woolly Ram, fleece brushed and fluffed, poses beside a big spread-out Starfish at the fair — pure BEAUTY.
reading_story: Bee hovers over the blooming garden, drawn to its BEAUTY.

story: Under the clamped Pot Lid, a Sealed Clam-Locket curls shut, hiding something tiny and unformed — cradled gently atop the glowing Full Moon, which nurses it patiently through the night until it's ready to BRING UP.
reading_story: Goalkeeper Iker cups the newborn in his gloved hands like a shot he refuses to drop, gently coaching it — this is how you BRING UP a champion.
issues: Full Moon actor 'nurses it patiently through the night until it's ready' attributes an intentional caretaking/cognitive role beyond its defined nature (glowing disc with surface stripes) — borderline personification, acceptable but worth tightening to a more passive/physical verb (e.g. 'glows over it').

story: The Full Moon hires two hands for a talent show: the Soup Ladle scoops a glowing dipper of moonlight, and the Sealed Clam-Locket clamps down to hoard it — moon's ABILITY: turning helpers into hoarded light.
reading_story: Backstage, Noah watches the Ladle pour light straight into the Clam-Locket's shut mouth, no spill — Noah whistles low: that hoarding trick is real ABILITY.

story: The Still Butte stands unmoved through every storm, weathered but GOOD, solid as the day it formed.
reading_story: Ryo grades the wine a solid GOOD, nodding with quiet approval.

story: A GRASS TUFT sprig tucked behind the ear like a stylish crown, while a hand pointing right (concept: right) checks it's angled just so — vain and YOUNG.
reading_story: Jacker rips a GRASS TUFT off a fence, chewing it cocky and YOUNG — he's never acted his age.

story: A leaf drifts past the Grass Tuft, past an Open Mouth catching raindrops, down through Puddle Splash, leaving one last Trailing Footprint as it hits the ground: FALL.
reading_story: Lacker watches the leaves FALL outside his window, one by one, all autumn long.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the Tree's canopy, each generation of growth stacking ring on ring beneath — every new sprout is one fresh LEAF.
reading_story: Yoyo twirls a single fallen LEAF between her fingers before letting it drift away.

story: At the center of the Four-Way Junction, a lone Tree grows, one perfect Ink Droplet caught frozen mid-fall from its highest branch — a still-life of pure ART.
reading_story: Jootter grunts as he hauls his canvas to the junction, determined to capture real ART.

story: The Hanger Kimono hangs empty, sleeves spread, only its silk shell showing — beside it the War Helmet rests hollow on its stand, just an outer shape with nothing inside. Both are pure SURFACE.
reading_story: Hugo peers into the empty War Helmet on its stand, frowns, and writes: appearances alone, everything on the SURFACE, nothing underneath.

story: On the windowsill, the Setting-Sun Cage glows red above; below it stands the Hourglass, sand streaming through its pinched waist. Between sunset and sand's end — that's the one moment you truly NEED.
reading_story: Yoyo draws his bow long and slow — ō, ō — while the Hourglass sand keeps falling. What you truly NEED, like his note, cannot be clipped short.

story: A HUSBAND stretches both arms straight out wide, fingertips taut, while the Periscope's eye-lens presses right against his fingertip, sighting dead level along his arms to mark the exact STANDARD.
reading_story: Key stands balanced on the husband's outstretched fingertip, dangling level and still — the locksmith's clipped "kee" note holding steady as the tiny proof that this arm-span meets the STANDARD.

story: Periscope rises and swivels its lens: up on the wire perches Stumpy Sparrow, a Feathered Arrow lodged beside it, framing the whole scenic OUTLOOK.
reading_story: Khan reins his horse atop the ridge, surveying the valley's OUTLOOK below.

story: The Cleaver hacks a cow's Sawn Antler free from the hide, prying the pieces apart strand by strand to UNRAVEL it all.
reading_story: Kai the surfer picks apart a tangled wetsuit strap to UNRAVEL it, muttering a short, clipped 'kai' with each tug.

story: Speech Bubble talks on and on — until it reaches the already-lowered Stop Barrier and can go no further, its last words pinned right there forever: a SCRIBE only writes down what stops.
reading_story: Key holds still at the lowered Stop Barrier, waiting; only what halts beside him gets written down as the SCRIBE's entry.

story: A Speech Bubble knocks twice, floats through the open door, and settles at the kitchen table — that's how you CALL ON an old friend.
reading_story: Ho drops by unannounced every Sunday, his booming laugh the first sign he's come to CALL ON you.

story: The judge squints at the Speech Bubble on the witness stand, its lid popping open — she leans in, studies every stacked word inside, and finally nods: RECOGNIZE.
reading_story: Ninn reads the Speech Bubble's stacked lines aloud in court, and the room comes to RECOGNIZE the voice at once.

story: Elder brother stands flanked by Twin Pillars like a podium, Speech Bubble ballooning above his head as he broadcasts his OPINION to the crowd below.
reading_story: Settler Seth climbs onto a podium built between Twin Pillars, clears his throat, and declares his own bold OPINION to the whole town.

story: Speech Bubble lifts her own lid, fans out the stacked word-lines like piano keys, and presses each one until the pitches match. TUNE.
reading_story: Cho presses Speech Bubble's stacked word-lines like keys, adjusting each until they ring in perfect TUNE.
issues: Reading_story largely re-stages the same 'press word-lines like keys' image as the main story instead of giving Cho a distinguishing action of his own — weakens distinctiveness between the meaning-story and reading-story pegs (rubric #10).

Speech Bubble is described as 'lifting her own lid' and 'fanning out' her own word-lines to tune herself, which is a slight departure from the registry persona's description (a bubble someone points at) — she becomes self-tuning rather than being acted on; check this reads as in-character.

周 (phonetic_extra) is silently dropped, which is allowed by the gates (not a mandatory component) but means the story does nothing to reinforce the phonetic link — acceptable per spec, flagging only for awareness.

story: Bonfire crackles beside the Speech Bubble, sparks popping like heated words flying back and forth — friends around the fire DISCUSS late into the night.
reading_story: Dan pokes the Bonfire, sending words flying from the Speech Bubble as everyone starts to DISCUSS his wild story.

story: The Speech Bubble shouts over the Attic Ledger Loft, pointing down at the neat rows of bound ledgers — voices clash into ARGUMENT.
reading_story: Ron climbs into the Attic Ledger Loft to settle the ARGUMENT, reading each ledger's cord-tied spine aloud until the shouting stops.

story: A Speech Bubble booms out one clear sound, while a Barbed Pike props up to stand up tall against the midday Sun, marking the line between right and wrong — sharp, DISCRIMINATING judgment.
reading_story: Shicker weighs every clue with sharp, DISCRIMINATING care before rendering his verdict.

story: The Speech Bubble's lid SLAMS open and its stacked words blare out sharp and repeated, jabbing at you like a finger — the crowd freezes, scolded. ADMONISH.
reading_story: Cabaret dancer Kayo drops her act mid-song, jabs a finger at the rowdy table, and lets her voice crack like a whip: ADMONISH them, Kayo!
issues: Reading_story keyword placement is slightly loose: 'ADMONISH them, Kayo!' trails the keyword with two more words rather than ending cleanly on it — acceptable but not crisp.
'jabbing at you like a finger' in the main story is a simile, not a literal added limb, but it's the shakiest phrase gate-wise; keep an eye on this pattern in future candidates for this actor.

story: Speech Bubble hovers left, chairing the session. On the right, Woolly Ram perches on the shoulders of the Pike-Wielding Duelist, who thrusts his pike declaring "this one's mine!" — sparking a heated DELIBERATION.
reading_story: Gee bangs the gavel, silencing the Duelist's boast: "Order — we settle this by DELIBERATION, not by pike."

story: The Swaddling Wrap curls tight from above, squeezing the Cowrie Shell in its one arm until the coin-shell cracks and every coin spills out empty-handed: DEFEAT.
reading_story: Foo bets his last cowrie shell, loses it in one short "fu" of a sigh, and slinks off in DEFEAT — no fight left, no shell left.

story: Twin Bowstrings twang taut over the Cowrie Shell, snapping again and again until the shell cracks and coins scatter loose — every shot is an EXPENSE.
reading_story: Hee giggles, watching coins fly everywhere: "hee hee, that's a huge EXPENSE!"

story: A Lightning Bolt cracks down, an Open Mouth roars, and the Conveyor Belt speeds up beneath them both — the CHASE is on.
reading_story: Twee sprints after the runaway kite in a breathless CHASE across the park.

story: The Conveyor Belt drags the rigid Still Butte backward off the platform edge — it won't budge an inch, yet the belt hauls it clean away in RETREAT.
reading_story: Ty steps back off the plate, refusing the pitch — a stubborn, clipped RETREAT rather than swing and risk the out.

story: The Cartwheel rolls onto the Conveyor Belt and rides it steadily forward, wheel and belt moving down the road as one — CONNECTED.
reading_story: Wren notices the wheel riding the belt without ever falling behind, clipping his short 'ren' each time they CONNECT.

story: Stumpy Sparrow, too fat and grumpy to fly, perches on the Conveyor Belt, which grinds along the road beneath him, dragging the stubborn old bird forward — he must ADVANCE.
reading_story: Shinn, the night bartender, watches the clock hands ADVANCE past closing time, sighing as he wipes one more glass before he can finally lock up.

story: The Goalpost Frame stands empty as an Open Mouth screams through its crossbar, both riding the Conveyor Belt straight past the posts, never stopping — OVERDOING it.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr floors the Conveyor Belt past the goalpost, meter still running long after the fare's done — he can't stop OVERDOING it.

story: Conveyor Belt hauls a Mound of Soil and a chewing Woolly Ram side by side down the line, grinding on and on — until both finally REACH the far end together.
reading_story: Tatum jogs the conveyor's length past soil and ram, arms pumping, determined to REACH the finish line first.

story: Two crates ride the Conveyor Belt side by side, twins in every way — until it dips and one tips sideways while the other stays upright. Now they're not twins. Pure DIFFERENCE.
reading_story: The belt dips — Eaton yelps "ee!" as his crate tips — his neighbor's stays level. He points at the DIFFERENCE between them.

story: Two Railway Tracks lead to a lowered Stop Barrier — no one may pass. A Lightning Bolt cracks down, snapping the crowd's Wishbone-shaped tension, and the Conveyor Belt alone carries the winner through. They ELECT.
reading_story: Senna alone gets waved past the Stop Barrier while the rest of the grid stays parked — the officials ELECT him first.

story: An Open Mouth props up to stand up tall on the left, roaring into the Staircase Curb's terraced steps on the right — each stacked step fences off its own SECTION.
reading_story: Boo climbs the Staircase Curb, claiming the top stack as his own private SECTION, barking a short 'bu' from the highest step.

story: The Staircase Curb sits fixed on one hillside road — yet every road in the land dead-ends at these same three rounded steps, the single doorstep of the whole METROPOLIS.
reading_story: Toto stands atop the Staircase Curb and shouts "To! To! To!" — three barks, one per step — echoing off every building of the METROPOLIS below.

story: The Corked Wine Jug stands beside the lowered Stop Barrier, and from behind its sealed neck, arms reach over the striped bar, handing out cups to everyone waiting in line: DISTRIBUTE.
reading_story: Hyde crouches by the Corked Wine Jug at the lowered Stop Barrier, doling out rations to the line of commuters — Mr. Hyde himself made to DISTRIBUTE.

story: A snapping Wishbone splits the air above a flat Horizon Line, where a huge Starfish sprawls arms-wide, bridging both sides — the barrier itself becomes the CONNECTION.
reading_story: Khan reins his horse hard at the barrier, but the Starfish's arm links his side to the guard's — even Khan can't refuse this CONNECTION.

story: The Terraced Hill's path climbs, ledge by ledge — but at the top stands the Still Butte, flat and unmoving, refusing all passage. This is the LIMIT: however high you climb, the rooted butte says no further.
reading_story: Hikers plead with Glenn, the trail warden guarding the Still Butte's ledge. Glenn shakes his head: this is the LIMIT, no permits issued past this terrace.

story: Falling Katana slices to show two Railway Tracks fading into a Sand Trickle at the cliff's brink, where Splayed Snowshoes stand planted right at the Terraced Hill's very EDGE.
reading_story: Cy Young toes the mound's very EDGE, cleats scraping the chalk line, never stepping past it.

story: A Grass Tuft sprouts over a grumpy Stumpy Sparrow pinned beneath a big Starfish, its Open Mouth clamped shut by a stubborn Pot Lid — escaping this mess is DIFFICULT.
reading_story: Nanny wrangles five toddlers into their coats at once — always DIFFICULT, she sighs with a short, clipped 'nan.'

story: Two mirrored wing-like strokes splay outward from a center line, neither matching the other — a perfect symbol for UN-, opposite and apart.
reading_story: Hee shakes his head firmly — 'UN-invited,' he says, turning the guest away.

story: A carnival clerk stamps a square MASK onto a customer's bare FACE — its surface printed with painted FEATURES: two round eyes, a nose ridge, a painted smile, all pressed flat against real skin.
reading_story: Menn buys the printed MASK at the stall, presses its flat surface to his face, and grins through the painted features — nose to nose with himself.

story: Cracked Conch shell balances upright on top like a crown — that spiral tip IS the HEAD.
reading_story: Tone Loc leans his HEAD back and drawls a long "tōoo" into the mic, milking the note.

story: Atop the MARBLE BUST, oneself's own face stares out — hair swept like Twin Pillars flanking the crown, the Watching Eye fixed dead ahead. Chin high, unmoving: this is the NECK.
reading_story: Master Shu grips the Marble Bust by its NECK, turning the stone head to check his own reflection in its watching eye.
issues: The 'hair swept like Twin Pillars flanking the crown' link for 并 is a bit forced/abstract — spatial role of 并 relative to the bust is not crisply visualized.
Slightly ambiguous how 'oneself's own face' (自) relates spatially to the marble bust — reads as grafted on rather than integrated.
